financials.source: Form 990 FY2024 (EIN 44-0605373) via ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer; total revenue $2.08B, total expenses $1.81B; operating budget reported as $1.7B by Children's Mercy; total assets $3.349B with net assets of approximately $2.7B

balanceSheetWealth.investmentPortfolioSource: Unrestricted cash and investments including hospital foundation holdings of $2.6B as of March 31, 2024, per Moody's and S&P credit reports cited in Beacon News and Healthcare Finance News
balanceSheetWealth.notes: Children's Mercy Hospital Foundation held $308M in total assets (FY2024). The Endowment Fund (EIN 44-6006542) contained 362 individual funds totaling $322M as of FY2025. Hospital plans to pay $1B+ of a $1.7B campus expansion in cash, indicating substantial liquid reserves beyond operational needs.

bondDebt.largestIssueProceeds: Estimated $250M–$350M; hospital seeking up to $500M in total new tax-exempt debt for $1.7B campus expansion, which would nearly triple existing debt load
bondDebt.issuerAuthority: Missouri Health and Educational Facilities Authority
bondDebt.source: Beacon News June 2026; Bond Buyer; Moody's and S&P reports on 2026 bond offering

relatedOrganizations.captiveInsurance: Childrens Mercy Hospital Self Insurance Trust (EIN 43-6321807)
relatedOrganizations.physicianGroupEntity: Children's Mercy - Pediatric Associates, Inc.; Children's Mercy - Preferred Pediatrics, Inc.
otherRelatedEntities: Childrens Mercy Family Health Partners Inc (EIN 43-1726517)
PedsMarket LLC (wholly owned subsidiary for pediatric innovation commercialization)
relatedOrganizations.source: Schedule R; ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer; Children's Mercy Center for Pediatric Innovation website

executiveComp.source: Form 990 FY2024 via ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer and GiveFreely; Kempinski retired effective January 2025; Dr. Alejandro Quiroga (formerly of Corewell Health) succeeded him as President and CEO effective January 2, 2025

communityBenefit.source: Children's Mercy FY2025 Community Benefit Report (childrensmercy.org); $352.8M total community benefit including $215.1M in uncompensated care; provides 100% charity care for Missouri and Kansas residents at or below 300% FPL

taxAdvantage.notes: Children's Mercy is tax-exempt since February 1956. Seeking up to $500M in new tax-exempt bonds in 2026 for campus expansion. Specific foregone tax amounts not verified.

layoffs.notes: Offered early retirement to an undisclosed number of employees among its approximately 9,000-person workforce; hospital leaders stated the voluntary retirement offer was unrelated to its $1.7 billion building expansion plans; number of eligible employees and projected payroll savings not disclosed
layoffs.source: Beacon News June 12, 2026; Springfield Business Journal

keyRiskFactors: $1.7 billion campus expansion could nearly triple existing debt load — Moody's warned significant complications could lead to downgrade
Stand-alone pediatric hospital with regional concentration in Kansas City metro
Up to $500M in new tax-exempt bond issuances planned for 2026
Workforce restructuring via early retirement offers concurrent with massive capital plan

acquisitions.notes: Children's Mercy officially took over leadership of pediatric specialty care in southwest Missouri through a partnership with Mercy Health Springfield; not a full acquisition but an operational takeover of pediatric services
$152 million expansion plan for Children's Mercy Hospital Kansas campus in Overland Park

ratios.investmentsToOperatingIncomeInterpretati: Operating income not separately verified from Form 990; total excess of revenue over expenses was approximately $270M (FY2024), which would yield a ratio of approximately 9.6x ($2.6B investments / $270M excess)
ratios.bondDebtToCommunityBenefitInterpretation: Total outstanding bond debt not verified; new issuances of up to $500M planned for 2026 campus expansion
ratios.charityCareVsStateInterpretation: Missouri state average not verified; Children's Mercy provides 100% charity care for residents at or below 300% FPL and claimed $215M in uncompensated care (FY2025)

accusation: Holds $2.6 billion in cash and investments atop $3.3 billion in total assets with an AA credit rating, yet offered early retirement to an undisclosed number of its 9,000 employees while seeking $500 million in new tax-exempt bonds to finance a $1.7 billion campus expansion that Moody's warned could triple its debt load.
